rv.q: This is Only a Test will weigh on your mind, and hopefully provoke conversations about solutions that are not militaristic or fear-based.
There are a lot of interesting ideas floated in This Is Only a Test , and lord knows the topic remains sadly relevant.
Eric Reyes Loo has written a play that provokes many ideas but just isn’t satisfying as a theatrical event.

Scenes and dialogue are often sorely in need of trimming in the interest of dramatic clarity, and strands of story are introduced needlessly, such as one involving litigation and another around inscription.
This new play has some promise, and it takes on a target I've never seen addressed, but it definitely still needs work.
“This Is Only a Test” could have been a marvelous satire, but it misses the mark.

cn.t: This timely satire about active shooter drills earns mixed reviews, with critics finding the premise provocative but execution uneven. Most praise its relevance while questioning its dramatic impact.
